feature.title: Driver Route Planning & Live Trajectory Visualization
feature.description: Before going on route, a driver sets their destination. The map computes and displays the optimized road trajectory using OSRM (free, no API key). The admin can select any driver on the FleetMap and view their active route polyline, destination marker, and ETA in real time.

geocoding.why: 100% free, no API key, already consistent with the OpenStreetMap tile provider used in Leaflet maps
geocoding.rate_limit: 1 request/second — debounce input by 500ms before firing

routing.service: OSRM Public Demo Server (Open Source Routing Machine)
routing.why: Free, no API key, returns GeoJSON polyline + duration + distance. Consistent with open-source philosophy of the stack.
routing.production_note: For production at scale (10k+ users), self-host OSRM via Docker or upgrade to Mapbox Directions API. Interface is identical — only the base URL changes.

map_rendering.polyline: react-leaflet <Polyline> component with GeoJSON coordinates array
map_rendering.destination_marker: Custom Leaflet divIcon with terracotta flag pin

new_table.name: driver_routes

columns.name: driver_id
columns.notes: indexed, one active route per driver

columns.name: destination_label
columns.notes: human-readable destination name e.g. 'Lyon Central Depot'

columns.name: route_geometry
columns.notes: GeoJSON LineString geometry from OSRM — { type: 'LineString', coordinates: [[lng,lat],...] }

columns.name: duration_seconds
columns.notes: OSRM estimated travel time in seconds at departure

columns.name: eta
columns.notes: computed as created_at + duration_seconds. Refreshed on significant GPS deviation.

new_table.unique_constraint: (driver_id) WHERE status = 'active' — only one active route per driver at a time (partial unique index)
new_table.migration_command: npm run db:generate && npm run db:migrate

new_api_routes.description: Driver sets a new active route. Calls OSRM server-side to compute the trajectory, persists to driver_routes, publishes Ably event.
server_actions: 1. Validate body with Zod RouteSetSchema (destinationLabel min 2 chars, lat/lng range checks)
3. GET current driver GPS from driver_locations table (must have a location — return 422 if null)
4. Fetch OSRM route server-side: GET https://router.project-osrm.org/route/v1/driving/{originLng},{originLat};{destLng},{destLat}?overview=full&geometries=geojson&steps=false with User-Agent header
5. Parse response: extract geometry, duration, distance from routes[0]
6. Upsert driver_routes: UPDATE existing active route to status='cancelled' if exists, then INSERT new row with status='active'
8. ablyPublish('fleet:locations', 'driver_route_set', { driverId, driverName, destinationLabel, destinationLat, destinationLng, eta, distanceMeters, durationSeconds, routeGeometry })
9. Return { routeId, eta, distanceMeters, durationSeconds, routeGeometry }
error_cases: 422 if driver has no GPS location yet — they must broadcast location first
502 if OSRM is unreachable — return error 'Could not compute route, please try again'
400 if OSRM returns no routes (unreachable destination)

new_api_routes.description: Get the current driver's active route. Used by the map page on mount to restore state.
Driver clears their active route (arrived or cancelled). Updates status to 'completed' or 'cancelled' based on query param ?reason=arrived|cancelled.
server_actions: 2. UPDATE status to completed/cancelled, set updated_at

new_api_routes.description: Admin fetches the active route for a specific driver to display on FleetMap.
server_actions: 2. Query driver_routes WHERE driver_id = driverId AND status = 'active'
3. JOIN users to get driverName, profileImageUrl
5. Return full route object including routeGeometry, eta, remainingSeconds, destinationLabel, driverName

new_api_routes.description: Returns a lightweight summary of all active driver routes (no geometry). Used for the admin FleetMap driver list sidebar to show which drivers have an active route.
new_api_routes.response: { routes: { driverId, driverName, destinationLabel, eta, distanceMeters, status }[] }

schemas.name: RouteSetSchema
schemas.zod: z.object({ destinationLabel: z.string().min(2).max(200), destinationLat: z.number().min(-90).max(90), destinationLng: z.number().min(-180).max(180) })

schemas.name: GeocodeResultSchema
schemas.zod: z.object({ place_id: z.number(), display_name: z.string(), lat: z.string(), lon: z.string() })

new_events.payload: { driverId, driverName, destinationLabel, destinationLat, destinationLng, eta (ISO string), distanceMeters, durationSeconds, routeGeometry (GeoJSON) }
consumers: Admin FleetMap — overlays route when the relevant driver is selected
Admin FleetMap — removes route overlay for that driver

subagents.name: Backend Route Agent
subagents.title: Database schema, API routes, OSRM integration, Ably events

instructions: Export async function fetchOsrmRoute(originLat, originLng, destLat, destLng): Promise<OsrmRouteResult>
OsrmRouteResult type: { geometry: GeoJSON.LineString, distanceMeters: number, durationSeconds: number }
Construct URL: `https://router.project-osrm.org/route/v1/driving/${originLng},${originLat};${destLng},${destLat}?overview=full&geometries=geojson&steps=false`
Fetch with headers: { 'User-Agent': 'TruckNet/1.0', 'Accept': 'application/json' }
Set fetch timeout: 8 seconds using AbortController
Parse response: if routes.length === 0 throw new Error('NO_ROUTE_FOUND')
Return routes[0].geometry, routes[0].distance, routes[0].duration
Wrap in try/catch — rethrow with typed error codes: 'OSRM_TIMEOUT', 'OSRM_UNREACHABLE', 'NO_ROUTE_FOUND'
Export a second helper: formatEta(durationSeconds: number): Date — returns new Date(Date.now() + durationSeconds * 1000)
Export formatDistance(meters: number): string — returns '0.4 km' if < 1000m, 'x.x km' if >= 1km
Export formatDuration(seconds: number): string — returns '14 min' or '1h 23min'
Add routeStatusEnum = pgEnum('route_status', ['active', 'completed', 'cancelled'])
Add driverRoutes table with all columns listed in database_changes.new_table
routeGeometry column: json('route_geometry').notNull() — stores GeoJSON object directly
Add partial unique index in a separate pgIndex export: unique on driver_id WHERE status = 'active'
Run npm run db:generate && npm run db:migrate after schema change
Handle GET: requireSession, query driverRoutes WHERE driverId = session.user.id AND status='active', return route or null

Handle POST: requireSession, parse and validate body with RouteSetSchema, get driver's last GPS from driver_locations (422 if not found), call fetchOsrmRoute from lib/osrm.ts, if throws NO_ROUTE_FOUND return 400 { error: 'No route to this destination' }, if throws OSRM_TIMEOUT/UNREACHABLE return 502 { error: 'Routing service unavailable, please try again' }, on success: UPDATE existing active routes to cancelled, INSERT new driverRoutes row, ablyPublish('fleet:locations', 'driver_route_set', payload), return 201 with route data

Handle DELETE: requireSession, query param ?reason=arrived|cancelled (default cancelled), UPDATE driverRoutes SET status=reason WHERE driverId AND status=active, ablyPublish driver_route_cleared, return 200

Handle GET: requireAdminSession(), extract driverId from params, query driverRoutes JOIN users WHERE driver_id=driverId AND status=active, compute remainingSeconds = Math.max(0, Math.floor((eta.getTime() - Date.now()) / 1000)), return full route view or null

Handle GET: requireAdminSession(), query all driverRoutes JOIN users WHERE status=active, return lightweight array (NO routeGeometry in this response — geometry is only fetched when admin selects a specific driver)
After the existing GPS upsert and Ably publish, add: query driver's active route from driverRoutes
If active route exists, check if driver has arrived: haversineDistanceKm(currentLat, currentLng, route.destinationLat, route.destinationLng) < 0.3 (300m threshold)
If within 300m: auto-complete the route — UPDATE status='completed', ablyPublish driver_route_cleared { driverId, reason: 'arrived' }
This auto-arrival detection runs on every GPS update without any driver action needed

cross_cutting_rules: OSRM is called server-side only (in API routes) — never directly from the browser, to avoid CORS and to keep the User-Agent header consistent
Nominatim is called via the /api/geocode proxy — never directly from browser
GeoJSON coordinates from OSRM are [longitude, latitude] — always reverse to [latitude, longitude] for Leaflet
Route geometry stored as jsonb in PostgreSQL — never stringify before insert, Drizzle handles serialization
Only ONE active route per driver enforced by partial unique index — the API must cancel previous route before inserting
Admin can only VIEW routes — they cannot create, modify, or cancel a driver's route
Auto-arrival detection runs in POST /api/drivers/location — no separate cron or worker needed
RoutePolyline and DestinationPin are shared components in components/map/ — imported by both driver DriverMap and admin DriverRouteOverlay
The preview endpoint must NOT write to DB or publish Ably events — it is read-only
formatDistance, formatDuration, formatEta helpers live in lib/osrm.ts and are importable by both server and client code
verification_steps: Driver opens map with no active route — 'Set Destination' button visible, no polyline shown
Driver searches 'Lyon' — Nominatim results appear in dropdown within 1 second of stopping typing
Driver selects destination — preview shows distance, duration, ETA before confirming
Driver clicks 'Start Route' — polyline appears on map, RouteInfoBar shows stats, button changes to 'On Route'
Driver refreshes page — GET /api/drivers/route restores route state, polyline redrawn
Admin opens /admin, clicks driver pin — 'View Route' button visible only for drivers with active routes
Admin clicks 'View Route' — slate polyline drawn, RouteInfoPanel card appears with ETA countdown
Admin clicks a different driver with a route — first route cleared, second route shown
Driver arrives within 300m of destination — route auto-completes, admin sees route_cleared event, overlay disappears
Driver manually clears route — polyline removed, button resets, admin overlay cleared via Ably
